01 / Why this location is interesting

It sits inside a dense movement network.

The site is on the Shudehill / NOMA side of Manchester city centre: close to Shudehill Interchange, Manchester Victoria, NOMA, the Northern Quarter, hotels, the Arndale retail core and major event traffic.

Important: this pack separates sourced city/location facts from my own planning estimates. I have not claimed measured doorstep footfall where I do not have a counter.

03 / Footfall planning estimate

Do not fake precision.

Manchester City Council publishes 90,500 weekday, 147,500 Saturday and 67,200 Sunday footfall for Market Street — the prime city retail benchmark, not Shudehill.

Planning estimate · not measured
4.5k–13.5k

Potential daily pass-by range

A deliberately broad planning range equal to ~5–15% of the published Market Street weekday benchmark. It is a hypothesis for budgeting, not a claimed site count.

How I'd turn the guess into data

  • 7-day manual or privacy-safe people count by hour.
  • Separate pedestrians, bus-stop dwellers, hotel flows and vehicle visibility.
  • Record frontage views → QR scans → page starts → qualified customers.
  • Calculate cost per incremental customer and K30 by physical-source cohort.
  • Kill it quickly if the site does not beat the acquisition benchmark.

Victoria proximity

NOMA describes Manchester Victoria as essentially on the neighbourhood's doorstep.

Nearby parking spaces

NOMA states approximately 3,000 car-parking spaces within a five-minute walk.

The road itself is media.

The frontage can generate impressions from pedestrians, bus users and passing traffic even when nobody walks inside. I would measure those separately rather than bundle them into a vague “footfall” number.

Not a clinic. A measurable physical acquisition surface.

08 / Where this belongs in my application

Supplementary. Not the pitch.

The core problem is still K30: 0.0835 → 0.30+. This facility is simply an unfair little advantage I already have access to: a place where I can turn an idea into a real-world experiment without first finding a landlord, venue or pop-up partner.

I would only deploy it if the data and compliance case made sense.

09 / Suggested 14-day pilot

Small enough to kill. Useful enough to learn.

Days 1–3

Count baseline movement, define audience windows, install attribution.

Days 4–7

Run 2–3 compliant window hooks and measure engagement.

Days 8–12

Keep winner, test QR vs tablet and visitor messaging.

Days 13–14

Compare cost, qualified starts, customers, retention signal and downstream K30 cohort.

Decision: scale, iterate or close it. The shop is not precious. The learning is.
